retro:
# Retrospective, PR #12984

## Worked

Bounded security triage included the linked issue before reviewer launch. Team ownership and managed Herdr context were checked before lifecycle control. Both reviewers used verified fresh exact-model sessions, received equivalent neutral scope and current corrections, and saved independent finals before coordinator read either. Source tracing answered the narrow integration question without real credentials or live desktop execution. A no-important-findings result remained acceptable. The final draft uses a small before/after table and explicitly source-only verification.

## Process deviation and remediation

Opus's synthetic run retained case-level streams but not nested backend raw streams/caller-observed exit status. It checked case completion but did not assert semantic outcomes. The upfront checklist acknowledged production stderr redirection without fixing retention. These omissions violate the complete per-child evidence gate. The run and original report remain intact, with a separate audit-addendum.md. Coordinator excluded its runtime observations from all public verification claims. Independent source evidence fully supports the final scoped conclusion, so this process-only deviation does not block publication.

Assignment corrections for future reviewers: a backend spawned by production must have raw streams retained from launch and its status recorded by a supervisor. Stub self-reporting does not satisfy the caller-side gate. Expected semantic output must fail explicitly on mismatch; nonempty stdout and exit zero are not semantic assertions. List every nested child in the final-target/producer checklist and reject a plan that leaves output redirected to an unretained sink. Apply this before execution, not after a seal.

No further native experiment could change an important retained public conclusion. The minor pre-existing EOF wording issue stayed local. No runtime claim is rescued by a seal or reviewer agreement.

## Tooling and cleanup

No confirmed tooling bug. Two unsupported Herdr help-discovery commands returned syntax errors and had no lifecycle effect, after which installed --help/--skill supplied the correct guidance. Reviewer process lifecycle stayed in Team 1. No host-visible process search, no system mutation or account query, no persistent memory edit, no upstream posting. The completed private sandbox namespace owns all fixture descendants and leaves no reserved resources. Saved HTML was not opened.

No important actionable issue found in the inspected scope at `3996942f`.

**Verified by source inspection:** both account RPCs now receive the same eight-second budget as initialization, and the descriptive exception reaches the panel through `authHelpText`.

| RPC setting | Before | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `initialize` | 8 seconds | 8 seconds |
| `account/read` | 4 seconds | 8 seconds |
| `account/rateLimits/read` | 4 seconds | 8 seconds |
| Timeout text | Bare method name | `Codex RPC timed out waiting for {method}` |

These are per-call budgets, not an eight-second total deadline. The inspected updater and panel impose no shorter timeout that would override them.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the collector, added tests, updater and panel integration. No runtime result is relied on here; the repository test suite, live panel and authenticated Codex behavior under load were not validated. Whether eight seconds is sufficient under real load remains unmeasured.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.
